title: Design a REST API
description: A shop is documenting POST /orders and retry behavior after a timeout. It wants predictable resource paths, status codes and method semantics. Which statement should guide the contract?

options.text: REST APIs should use verbs in URL paths (e.g., /getUsers, /deletePost)
options.explanation: REST uses nouns for resources (/users, /posts) and HTTP methods (GET, DELETE) for actions. Verbs in URLs is an anti-pattern.

options.text: Idempotency means repeating one logical operation has the same intended effect on server state as doing it once
options.explanation: GET, PUT and DELETE are idempotent in intended effect, not necessarily in response status: a second DELETE may return a different status. POST retries need a persisted, scoped idempotency key and atomic duplicate handling.

options.text: HTTP 200 is the correct status code for a successful resource creation
options.explanation: 201 Created is the correct status for successful resource creation. 200 OK is for successful retrieval or update operations.

options.text: GraphQL is a type of REST API
options.explanation: GraphQL is a separate query language and execution model, not a kind of REST. It often uses one endpoint and can use GET for queries as well as POST; endpoint count and POST alone do not define the distinction.
